- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) within 3–5 days, model overreacts with downward bias; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature sell-off.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive days of rising prices); add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to capture pullback.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly signals trend continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model tends to forecast mid-range; avoid extreme deviations; anchor forecast to 1–2% below recent 10-day average.
